is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles gambiae s.l. collected in Atatam, southern Ghana (Page 1-2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotyped target resistance markers including Vgsc-L1014F (L995F), Vgsc-L1014S (L995S), Vgsc-N1575Y (N1570Y), Ace-1 G119S (G280S), Rdl A296S, GSTe2 L119F, Ace-1 N485I, CYP6P9a, and CYP6P9b in field populations (Page 4, 7-8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Reports sample sizes and exact genotype/allele frequencies for F0 mosquitoes: e.g. RDL 296S in An. funestus (50 genotyped: 36 RR, 12 RS, 2 SS), GSTe2 L119F (53 genotyped: 16 RR, 25 RS, 12 SS), Ace-1 G119S in An. gambiae s.l. (35 genotyped: 16 RR, 3 RS, 16 SS), and Vgsc-1014F (38 F0 genotyped, allele frequency 90.79%) (Page 7-8).

african_field_population.evidence: Indoor blood-fed resting female Anopheles were collected in the village of Atatam, Ashanti Region, Southern Ghana in July and October 2021 (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting field mosquito collections, susceptibility bioassays, and molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: Atatam (06° 17.377″ N, 001° 27.545″ W), Adansi Asokwa District, Ashanti Region, Ghana (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in July and October 2021 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Fresh field collections conducted specifically for this study in 2021.

supplement.evidence: Sufficient extractable genotype counts and frequencies are reported directly in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide susceptibility, LLIN bio-efficacy, and resistance mechanisms in Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles gambiae s.l. from Atatam, Southern Ghana collected in 2021. Target-site markers (Vgsc-1014F, 1014S, 1575Y, Ace-1 G119S, Rdl A296S, Ace-1 N485I) and metabolic markers (GSTe2 L119F, CYP6P9a, CYP6P9b) were genotyped, providing extractable genotype frequencies and genotype-phenotype association data for survivors and dead mosquitoes post-exposure.
